text:
A group of crows is called a murder.

The text describes a classic social engineering tactic known as a Business Email Compromise (BEC) or spear-phishing attack. The attacker exploits urgency ("immediate action required") and authority (impersonating the CEO) to pressure employees into bypassing security protocols. By instructing staff to send sensitive customer data to an external email for "safekeeping," the attacker aims to steal data under the guise of protecting it, leveraging fear of data loss to manipulate compliance.
